description: Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao is a beloved Hong Kong classic, despite containing no actual pineapple in its dough or crispy, sweet topping. This iconic pastry features a soft, fluffy bread base crowned with a crumbly, sugary crust that resembles a pineapple's textured skin. Enjoy this delightful treat warm, often with a slice of butter tucked inside, for a truly authentic experience that captures the essence of Chinese baking.

ingredients.notes: for the bun dough, plus 1 for egg wash

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine bread flour, sugar, instant yeast, and salt. Add the egg and warm milk, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10-12 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate the softened butter and knead for another 5 minutes until the butter is fully absorbed and the dough is very smooth.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size. This step is crucial for developing the fluffy texture of the bun.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough proofs, cream together the softened butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and evaporated milk until well combined. Gradually add the all-purpose flour and baking powder, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. Divide this topping dough into 8 equal portions, rolling each into a ball, then flattening slightly into a disk.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the bun dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release air. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Take one flattened topping disk and gently place it over a bun dough ball, pressing lightly to adhere and cover about two-thirds of the bun's surface. Repeat for all buns.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Egg Wash
instructions.text: Place the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Whisk the remaining egg yolk with 1 teaspoon of water for the egg wash. Gently brush the egg wash over the pineapple topping of each bun.

instructions.title: Bake the Buns
instructions.text: Bake the Pineapple Buns in the preheated oven for 15-18 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through. The cracks in the topping are what give it the signature pineapple-like appearance.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the buns from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed warm, often sliced horizontally and served with a thick slice of cold butter tucked inside for a truly decadent treat.

tips: Ensure your butter for the topping is genuinely softened, not melted, for the best crumbly texture. Cold butter will make it hard to combine evenly.
Do not overwork the pineapple topping dough; mix just until combined to prevent it from becoming tough. The goal is a delicate, crumbly crust.
For an extra fragrant topping, you can add a tiny pinch of custard powder or vanilla extract to the pineapple topping mixture.
